title: Mathematics — Grade 6 Entrance
subject: math

questions.prompt:
Write a number in the box to make the statement correct.

1694 ÷ 100 = ______

Here is the spatial pattern for the first three triangular numbers (see Pattern 1, Pattern 2 and Pattern 3 in the picture).

Write the first three triangular numbers.

Carlos says, '34 is a multiple of 4'

Carlos is **not** correct.

Explain how you know that 34 is **not** a multiple of 4
questions.criteria: 1 point for a valid explanation, e.g.: 34 ÷ 4 leaves a remainder (34 ÷ 4 = 8 remainder 2); or 4 × 8 = 32 and 4 × 9 = 36, so 34 is not in the 4 times table; or halving 34 twice does not give a whole number (17 is odd). A bare statement with no reasoning earns 0.

questions.prompt: Write a 3-digit number that is divisible by 2
questions.answerKey: Any 3-digit even number (100–998 ending in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8), e.g. 100

questions.prompt:
The time in Manila is 18:40
The time in Sydney is 3 hours ahead of the time in Manila.

Work out the time in Sydney.

The children in Class 5 want to know if boys have bigger feet than girls.
They collect data.

Choose the data collection that is **least** useful.

choices.text: Measure the length of each person's shoe
Measure the length of each person's foot
Measure the width of each person's foot
Calculate the area of each person's foot

questions.prompt:
Here is a shape made of squares (see picture; the grey squares are shaded).

Shade **two** more squares so that the shape has exactly one line of symmetry.

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot draw, describe in words which two squares you would shade, e.g. by row and column.]
questions.criteria: The grid is 5 columns × 4 rows; shaded squares are at row 1 column 2, row 2 column 3, row 2 column 5 and row 4 column 2 (rows counted from the top). 1 point for shading (or clearly describing) the two squares at row 3 column 3 and row 3 column 5 — directly below the two shaded squares in row 2 — giving the shape exactly one (horizontal) line of symmetry. Accept any other pair only if it also results in exactly one line of symmetry.

questions.prompt:
Tick (✓) to show if each number is divisible by 2, 4 or 8
One number has been done for you.

| Number | Divisible by 2 | Divisible by 4 | Divisible by 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 116 |  |  |  |
| 126 |  |  |  |

[Type your answer for each row, e.g. "116: divisible by ... ; 126: divisible by ..."]
questions.answerKey: 116: divisible by 2 and 4 (not 8); 126: divisible by 2 only

questions.prompt: Write 8/3 as a mixed number.

Here is a shape drawn on a grid of squares (see picture — a black square on the grid).

The shape is translated 3 squares to the left.

Draw the translated shape on the grid.

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot draw, describe in words where the translated shape is.]
questions.criteria: 1 point for drawing (or clearly describing) an identical square 3 grid squares to the left of the original, same row and same size.

questions.prompt:
Work out.

1/4 + 1/8

Write True or False for each statement.

| # | Statement | True or False? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 + 3 + 4 = 4 + 6 + 3 |  |
| 2 | 16 × 2 = 10 × 2 + 6 × 2 |  |
| 3 | 5 − 3 = 3 − 5 |  |
| 4 | 36 × 5 = 4 × 8 × 5 |  |

[Type your answer as e.g. "1 True, 2 False, 3 ..., 4 ..."]

Here is the age and mass of five animals.

| Animal | A | B | C | D | E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Age (years) | 9 | 5 | 8 | 4 | 4 |
| Mass (kg) | 12 | 9 | 8 | 16 | 21 |

(a) Write the mode of the animal ages (in years).

Here is the age and mass of five animals.

| Animal | A | B | C | D | E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Age (years) | 9 | 5 | 8 | 4 | 4 |
| Mass (kg) | 12 | 9 | 8 | 16 | 21 |

(b) Write the median mass (in kg).

Here is a coordinate grid with point A marked (A is at (3, 2)).

Plot a **different** point that has the same y-coordinate as A. Label the point B.

[Instead of plotting, write the coordinates of your point B, e.g. (1, 2).]

Match the calculation 7 × 6 × 5 to **each** equivalent calculation.

The five calculations are:

- 6 × 35
- 7 × 36
- 7 × 2 × 3 × 5
- 21 × 10
- 48 × 5

[Write ALL of the calculations from the list that are equivalent to 7 × 6 × 5.]

A football team play 10 matches.
They win, lose or draw each match.

They win more matches than they lose.
They win more matches than they draw.
They draw more matches than they lose.
They lose 2 matches.

Complete the dot plot (2 dots are already shown for 'lose').

[Instead of drawing, write the number of dots for 'win' and for 'draw'.]

Youssef draws a right-angled isosceles triangle.

Choose the number of lines of symmetry Youssef's triangle has.

Mike buys 8 planks of wood.
Each plank has a length of 1.3 metres.

Work out the total length of the 8 planks of wood (in metres).

Oliver has 30 roses.
10 of the roses are red.
Some of the roses are white.
The rest of the roses are yellow.

Oliver picks a rose at random.

Oliver says, 'I am most likely to pick a yellow rose.'

Complete the table to make Oliver's statement correct.

| Colour of rose | Number of roses |
|---|---|
| Red | 10 |
| White |  |
| Yellow |  |

[Type the number of white roses and the number of yellow roses.]
questions.answerKey: White and Yellow must total 20 with Yellow more than 10 and more than White (and White at least 1), e.g. White 9, Yellow 11

questions.prompt:
A bag contains 12 pencils.
A box contains 156 bags of pencils.

Work out the number of pencils in a box.

Write a number in the box to make the sentence correct.

2.5 days = ______ hours

A bag contains exactly 2 red beads and 3 blue beads.

Write the correct number in each box to make the statement correct.

______ in every ______ beads in the bag are **blue**.

Here is a number.

14.26

Write, in words, the value represented by the digit 6

Lily has 636 beads.
She makes necklaces using the beads.
Each necklace uses 6 beads.

Work out the number of necklaces Lily can make.

Mia has a spinner with 8 equal sections.
Each section has the number 1 or 2 or 3 or 4 written on it.

Mia is more likely to spin a 3 than a 2
Mia is equally likely to spin a 2 or a 1
Mia is less likely to spin a 3 than a 4

Write a number in each section to complete Mia's spinner.

[Instead of writing on the spinner, type how many sections get each number, e.g. "two 1s, three 2s, ...".]
questions.answerKey: e.g. one 1, one 2, two 3s, four 4s — accept any filling of all 8 sections where the number of 1s equals the number of 2s, there are more 3s than 2s, and fewer 3s than 4s

questions.prompt:
Write a number in the box to make the statement correct.

14.07 × 100 ÷ 10 = ______ ÷ 100

Three different angles are joined to make a straight line.

Choose the **three** angles that could make the straight line.

10°   20°   30°   40°   90°   100°   110°

[Write the three angles.]

Angelique's watch is 12 minutes slower than Jamila's watch.
The time on Angelique's watch is 14:52

Write the time on Jamila's watch.

Here are two rectangles (not drawn to scale).

Rectangle 1 is 3 cm long and 2 cm high.
Rectangle 2 is 6 cm long and 2 cm high.

The two rectangles are joined together to make a new shape: the smaller rectangle sits on top of the larger rectangle (see picture).

Calculate the perimeter of the new shape (in cm).

Here is a grid of squares.

Draw **four** identical right-angled triangles arranged to make a larger right-angled triangle.

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot draw, describe your arrangement in words.]
questions.criteria: 1 point for four identical right-angled triangles drawn (or clearly described) so that together they form one larger right-angled triangle, e.g. a large right-angled triangle with legs twice those of the small triangle, divided into four congruent copies.

questions.prompt:
Mia asks 32 children which musical instrument they play.
The table shows her data.

| Instrument | Number of children |
|---|---|
| Piano | 16 |
| Violin | 10 |
| Drums | 6 |

The bar chart shows some of this information (the Piano bar is drawn, 8 grid squares tall; the y-axis has no scale yet).

Complete the bar chart by

- adding a scale to the y-axis
- drawing and labelling bars for violin and drums.

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot draw, describe the scale you would use and how tall each bar would be.]
questions.criteria: 1 point for a correct, consistent y-axis scale that makes the Piano bar read 16 (each grid square = 2 children, axis marked 2, 4, 6, ... 16 or equivalent). 1 point for violin and drums bars drawn/described at the correct heights (violin = 10, i.e. 5 squares; drums = 6, i.e. 3 squares) and labelled.
